request.question: When is a canary deployment rolled back automatically?

response.answer: Production deployments use canary releases managed by Argo Rollouts. [1] A canary is rolled back automatically if the error rate exceeds 1% or p99 latency regresses by more than 20%. [1] During the freeze only SEV-1 fixes may be deployed, and every deployment requires approval from the Incident Commander on duty. [2] Error budget burn above 2x for one hour pages the on-call engineer automatically. [3]

citations.title: Deployment Standards
citations.snippet: Production deployments use canary releases managed by Argo Rollouts. Traffic shifts 5%, 25%, 50%, then 100%, with automated analysis against Datadog metrics at each step. A canary is rolled back automatically if the error rate exceeds 1% or p99 latency regresses by more than 20%.

citations.title: Deployment Standards
citations.snippet: A change freeze applies from December 15 to January 5 every year. During the freeze only SEV-1 fixes may be deployed, and every deployment requires approval from the Incident Commander on duty.

citations.title: Payments Platform Architecture
citations.snippet: The Payments API has an availability SLO of 99.95% measured monthly. The p99 latency objective is 300 ms for authorization requests. Error budget burn above 2x for one hour pages the on-call engineer automatically.
